recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中央一顆極大的細胞，細胞質豐富且呈深藍色，核圓形、含明顯核仁，體積數倍於旁邊骨髓細胞，背景造血成熟正常，符合多發性骨髓瘤中的大型不典型漿細胞。
features: Single giant cell with abundant intensely basophilic cytoplasm
Large round nucleus with fine to slightly open chromatin and a visible nucleolus
Low to moderate N:C ratio; paranuclear hof not well defined
Adjacent cell with pale gray-blue cytoplasm abutting the large cell
Background trilineage hematopoiesis with maturing neutrophils, erythroid precursors and eosinophils
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a background of normal maturing granulocytic and erythroid precursors with a single markedly enlarged cell. The cell has abundant, intensely basophilic cytoplasm and a large round nucleus with relatively fine chromatin and a visible nucleolus, consistent with a large atypical or immature plasma cell. The perinuclear hof is not distinct. Correlation with CD138 staining, flow cytometric light chain restriction, and serum protein studies is required; findings are compatible with plasma cell myeloma with large atypical plasma cells.

ddx.vs: Osteoblasts usually appear in groups with a comet-shaped outline and a pale zone distant from the nucleus, and are CD138/cytoplasmic light chain negative.
Pronormoblasts are smaller with very high N:C ratio, cytoplasmic blebs and fine nuclear chromatin with multiple nucleoli, and are CD71/E-cadherin positive.
Metastatic cells are usually cohesive clusters with pleomorphic nuclei and are cytokeratin or other lineage-marker positive rather than CD138/light chain restricted.
